scope: Bounded server-only stateless blind-evaluation concurrency study on all 256 frozen new-development receiver visits.

workspace_policy.creation: serial on the main thread before worker threads start
workspace_policy.prewarm: one untimed run for every worker/geometry workspace before worker threads start, including lazy plan creation
workspace_policy.destruction: serial on the main thread after all worker threads join
workspace_policy.reason: FFTW planning and destruction are not assumed thread-safe; only execution of distinct plans is concurrent

primary_visit_modes.fp64_serial_pair: packed stable FP64 runs RX0 then RX1 on CPU0
primary_visit_modes.fp32_serial_pair: strided FP32 FFTW runs RX0 then RX1 on CPU0
primary_visit_modes.fp32_parallel_pair: persistent two-worker pool runs only RX0 and RX1 of one physical visit, waits for both, then advances; no queued next visit

secondary_batch_modes.backend: unchanged strided FP32 FFTW, unseeded, maximum=1
secondary_batch_modes.task_inventory: all 256 receiver visits exactly once per batch

measurement.mode_order: counterbalanced across repetitions; case order forward, reverse, then deterministic rotation
measurement.batch_wall: monotonic time from immediately before first direct call/task enqueue through final result compaction/collection
measurement.aggregate_process_cpu: process CPU over the same batch boundary, including all worker threads
measurement.summed_task_cpu: sum of thread CPU measured per task
measurement.task_latency: per receiver view formation, native detector call, and scientific result compaction
measurement.pair_latency: per physical visit boundary around two serial calls or two enqueue/result operations

validation.all_parallel_signatures: must exactly equal the serial FP32 signature for the same receiver visit
validation.reference_gate: all positive FP64/FP32 pairs must associate within circular timing <=2 us and CFO <=8 kHz; no lost or additional positives

interpretation: Batch throughput is not single-visit latency or a real-time guarantee.
Wall-throughput speedup is not aggregate-CPU speedup.
This stateless component benchmark is not an end-to-end pipeline speedup claim.
Server results do not establish ARM performance.
